column1: # Xenoblade Chronicles 3 on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Monolith Soft's engine on SDK 12.3.9, update 2.2.0 with its four DLC. On the Y700 (2026-10-26), driven with DM_CTL: boot, the title (lit dragon, foreground clouds),
# a new game, the opening movie (VP9) and skipping it (hold X), the first battles, the tutorials and the story to Torchlight Hill, saving and loading, and the pause
# menu's Performance / Resolution switch: 30 fps held (frame p50 33.3 ms, p95 34-35 ms) over 15 minutes of walking Everblight Plain, mappings steady at 15,000-19,000
# and GPU memory steady, no audio underruns. Heavy views of Torchlight Hill take about 40 ms a frame. The sky's cloud layer, which dropped out while the camera
# turned (Adreno applied another depth buffer's LRZ; fixed in the core, gfx_vk_exec.c pass_commit), stays on: 0 flicker frames in 3 turning recordings (2026-10-27).
# Speed (2026-10-27, CPU capped at ~2.0 GHz by the tablet): with the core fixes to the window acquire's sync, the submission slot ring and command buffers
# reset on the completion thread, and the replay on its own thread (env below), it holds 30 fps in Performance and Resolution mode, field and battle:
# frame p50 33.2 ms, p95 33.7-34.5 ms (Resolution-mode battles with ~2,800 draws included; they were 36 ms with the replay on the render thread).
# Thin black slivers over the cliffs and grass of Everblight Plain (2-6% of frames, the user's report of black flicker; 2026-10-27): its mesh-transforming
# vertex shaders ran unordered with the G-buffer draws on Adreno; fixed in the core (gfx_vk_exec.c prepare_draw): 0 in 6 recordings of 361 frames.
# Hundreds of its effect and model shaders are in no game file: the app captures each one a draw misses, and the next port with --install translates them
# (260 so far, 2026-10-27, from the opening, the first field and its battles); until then such draws are skipped, so the status is wip until the shaders are ported.
